translation.en: June 19
translation.kr: 6월 19일

raw: I no longer remember where I stopped in my narrative: I only know it was two in the morning when I went to bed; and if you had been with me, that I might have talked instead of writing to you, I should, in all probability, have kept you up till daylight.

translation.en: I no longer remember where I broke off in my account.
translation.kr: 이야기를 어디서 끊었는지 이제 기억나지 않네.

translation.en: I only know it was two in the morning when I went to bed; and if you had been here, so that I could talk instead of write, I would probably have kept you up till daylight.
translation.kr: 다만 잠자리에 든 것이 새벽 두 시였다는 것만 아네. 그리고 자네가 여기 있어서 쓰는 대신 말할 수 있었다면, 아마 날이 밝을 때까지 자네를 붙들어 두었을 걸세.

raw: I think I have not yet related what happened as we rode home from the ball, nor have I time to tell you now. It was a most magnificent sunrise: the whole country was refreshed, and the rain fell drop by drop from the trees in the forest. Our companions were asleep. Charlotte asked me if I did not wish to sleep also, and begged of me not to make any ceremony on her account. Looking steadfastly at her, I answered, "As long as I see those eyes open, there is no fear of my falling asleep." We both continued awake till we reached her door. The maid opened it softly, and assured her, in answer to her inquiries, that her father and the children were well, and still sleeping. I left her asking permission to visit her in the course of the day. She consented, and I went, and, since that time, sun, moon, and stars may pursue their course: I know not whether it is day or night; the whole world is nothing to me.

translation.en: I do not think I have told you yet what happened as we rode home from the ball, and I have no time to tell you now.
translation.kr: 무도회에서 돌아오는 길에 있었던 일은 아직 자네에게 말하지 않은 것 같네만, 지금은 말할 겨를이 없네.

translation.en: It was a magnificent sunrise.
translation.kr: 장엄한 해돋이였네.

translation.en: The whole country was fresh, and the rain fell drop by drop from the trees in the forest.
translation.kr: 온 들판이 싱그러웠고, 숲의 나무들에서는 빗방울이 한 방울씩 떨어지고 있었네.

translation.en: Our companions were asleep.
translation.kr: 동행들은 잠들어 있었네.

translation.en: Charlotte asked whether I did not want to sleep as well, and begged me not to stand on ceremony for her sake.
translation.kr: 샤를로테는 나도 자고 싶지 않으냐고 물으며, 자기 때문에 사양하지는 말라고 했네.

translation.en: Looking steadily at her, I answered, "As long as I can see those eyes open, there is no danger of my falling asleep."
translation.kr: 나는 그 사람을 똑바로 바라보며 답했네. "그 눈이 뜨여 있는 것을 보는 한, 제가 잠들 염려는 없습니다."

translation.en: We both stayed awake until we reached her door.
translation.kr: 우리 둘은 그 집 문 앞에 이를 때까지 깨어 있었네.

translation.en: The maid opened it softly and assured her, in answer to her questions, that her father and the children were well and still sleeping.
translation.kr: 하녀가 살며시 문을 열고, 아버지와 아이들 모두 잘 있으며 아직 자고 있다고 대답해 주었네.

translation.en: I left her, asking leave to visit her later in the day.
translation.kr: 나는 그날 낮에 찾아가도 좋겠느냐고 청하고 물러났네.

translation.en: She agreed, and I went; and since then the sun and moon and stars may go their own way.
translation.kr: 그 사람이 허락했고 나는 갔네. 그 뒤로 해도 달도 별도 제 갈 길을 가든 말든일세.

translation.en: I do not know whether it is day or night; the whole world is nothing to me.
translation.kr: 낮인지 밤인지도 모르겠고, 온 세상이 내게는 아무것도 아니네.

translation.en: June 21
translation.kr: 6월 21일

raw: My days are as happy as those reserved by God for his elect; and, whatever be my fate hereafter, I can never say that I have not tasted joy,—the purest joy of life. You know Walheim. I am now completely settled there. In that spot I am only half a league from Charlotte; and there I enjoy myself, and taste all the pleasure which can fall to the lot of man.

translation.en: My days are as happy as those God keeps for his elect.
translation.kr: 내 나날은 신이 당신께서 택하신 이들을 위해 간직해 두신 날들만큼이나 행복하네.

translation.en: And whatever my fate may be hereafter, I can never say that I have not tasted joy — the purest joy of life.
translation.kr: 그리고 앞으로 내 운명이 어찌 되든, 나는 기쁨을 — 삶의 가장 순수한 기쁨을 — 맛보지 못했다고는 결코 말하지 못할 걸세.

translation.en: You know Walheim.
translation.kr: 발하임을 자네도 알지.

translation.en: I am now completely settled there.
translation.kr: 나는 이제 그곳에 아주 자리를 잡았네.

translation.en: From that spot I am only half a league from Charlotte; and there I enjoy myself, and taste every pleasure that can fall to a man's lot.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 샤를로테까지는 겨우 오 리 남짓일세. 거기서 나는 즐겁게 지내며, 사람에게 돌아올 수 있는 온갖 기쁨을 맛보고 있네.

raw: Little did I imagine, when I selected Walheim for my pedestrian excursions, that all heaven lay so near it. How often in my wanderings from the hillside or from the meadows across the river, have I beheld this hunting-lodge, which now contains within it all the joy of my heart!

translation.en: Little did I imagine, when I chose Walheim for my walks, that all heaven lay so close to it.
translation.kr: 산책하려고 발하임을 골랐을 때만 해도, 온 천국이 그토록 가까이 있으리라고는 생각지도 못했네.

translation.en: How often, wandering from the hillside or across the meadows by the river, have I looked at this hunting-lodge, which now holds all the joy of my heart!
translation.kr: 언덕에서, 또는 강가 초원을 거닐며 이 사냥막을 얼마나 자주 바라보았던가. 이제는 그곳이 내 마음의 모든 기쁨을 품고 있네!

raw: I have often, my dear Wilhelm, reflected on the eagerness men feel to wander and make new discoveries, and upon that secret impulse which afterward inclines them to return to their narrow circle, conform to the laws of custom, and embarrass themselves no longer with what passes around them.

translation.en: I have often reflected, my dear Wilhelm, on the eagerness men feel to wander and make new discoveries.
translation.kr: 친애하는 빌헬름, 나는 자주 생각해 보았네. 사람들이 어찌하여 그토록 떠돌며 새것을 찾아다니고 싶어 하는지를.

translation.en: And on the secret impulse that afterwards draws them back to their narrow circle, to conform to custom, and to trouble themselves no further with what goes on around them.
translation.kr: 그리고 뒤에 가서는 어찌하여 어떤 은밀한 충동이 그들을 다시 좁은 테두리로 끌어들여, 관습에 순응하고 둘레에서 벌어지는 일에 더는 마음 쓰지 않게 만드는지를.

raw: It is so strange how, when I came here first, and gazed upon that lovely valley from the hillside, I felt charmed with the entire scene surrounding me. The little wood opposite—how delightful to sit under its shade! How fine the view from that point of rock! Then, that delightful chain of hills, and the exquisite valleys at their feet! Could I but wander and lose myself amongst them! I went, and returned without finding what I wished. Distance, my friend, is like futurity. A dim vastness is spread before our souls: the perceptions of our mind are as obscure as those of our vision; and we desire earnestly to surrender up our whole being, that it may be filled with the complete and perfect bliss of one glorious emotion. But alas! when we have attained our object, when the distant there becomes the present here, all is changed: we are as poor and circumscribed as ever, and our souls still languish for unattainable happiness.

translation.en: It is strange how, when I first came here and looked down on that lovely valley from the hillside, the whole scene around me charmed me.
translation.kr: 이상한 일일세. 처음 이곳에 와서 언덕에서 저 사랑스러운 골짜기를 내려다보았을 때, 둘레의 온 풍경이 나를 사로잡았네.

translation.en: The little wood opposite — how delightful to sit in its shade!
translation.kr: 맞은편 작은 숲 — 그 그늘에 앉으면 얼마나 좋을까!

translation.en: How fine the view from that point of rock!
translation.kr: 저 바위 끝에서 내려다보는 경치는 또 얼마나 근사할까!

translation.en: And that lovely chain of hills, with the exquisite valleys at their feet!
translation.kr: 그리고 발치에 더없이 고운 골짜기들을 거느린 저 사랑스러운 언덕 줄기!

translation.en: If only I could wander and lose myself among them!
translation.kr: 저 사이를 거닐며 나를 잃어버릴 수만 있다면!

translation.en: I went, and came back without finding what I wanted.
translation.kr: 가 보았네. 그리고 원하던 것을 찾지 못한 채 돌아왔네.

translation.en: Distance, my friend, is like the future.
translation.kr: 친구여, 먼 곳이란 미래와 같은 것일세.

translation.en: A dim vastness lies spread out before our souls.
translation.kr: 어슴푸레한 광막함이 우리 영혼 앞에 펼쳐져 있네.

translation.en: The perceptions of our mind are as blurred as those of our eyes, and we long to surrender our whole being, to have it filled with the complete and perfect bliss of one glorious feeling.
translation.kr: 우리 마음의 지각은 우리 눈의 지각만큼이나 흐릿하고, 우리는 존재 전체를 내맡겨 하나의 영광스러운 감정이 주는 완전하고 온전한 지복으로 채워지기를 갈망하네.

translation.en: But alas, when we have reached the thing, when the distant there has become the present here, everything is changed.
translation.kr: 그러나 아, 막상 그것에 다다르면, 저 먼 저곳이 지금 이곳이 되고 나면, 모든 것이 달라져 있네.

translation.en: We are as poor and as hemmed in as ever, and our souls still thirst for a happiness they cannot reach.
translation.kr: 우리는 여전히 가난하고 여전히 갇혀 있으며, 우리 영혼은 여전히 닿을 수 없는 행복에 목말라하네.

raw: So does the restless traveller pant for his native soil, and find in his own cottage, in the arms of his wife, in the affections of his children, and in the labour necessary for their support, that happiness which he had sought in vain through the wide world.

translation.en: So the restless traveller longs for his native soil.
translation.kr: 그렇게 떠돌던 나그네도 제 고향 땅을 그리워하게 되네.

translation.en: And he finds in his own cottage, in his wife's arms, in his children's affection, and in the work needed to keep them, the happiness he had searched the whole wide world for in vain.
translation.kr: 그리고 제 오두막에서, 아내의 품에서, 아이들의 정에서, 그들을 먹이기 위한 일에서, 온 세상을 헤매어도 헛되이 찾던 행복을 찾아내지.

raw: When, in the morning at sunrise, I go out to Walheim, and with my own hands gather in the garden the pease which are to serve for my dinner, when I sit down to shell them, and read my Homer during the intervals, and then, selecting a saucepan from the kitchen, fetch my own butter, put my mess on the fire, cover it up, and sit down to stir it as occasion requires, I figure to myself the illustrious suitors of Penelope, killing, dressing, and preparing their own oxen and swine. Nothing fills me with a more pure and genuine sense of happiness than those traits of patriarchal life which, thank Heaven! I can imitate without affectation. Happy is it, indeed, for me that my heart is capable of feeling the same simple and innocent pleasure as the peasant whose table is covered with food of his own rearing, and who not only enjoys his meal, but remembers with delight the happy days and sunny mornings when he planted it, the soft evenings when he watered it, and the pleasure he experienced in watching its daily growth.

translation.en: In the morning at sunrise I go out to Walheim and gather the peas in the garden with my own hands for my dinner.
translation.kr: 아침 해가 뜰 무렵 나는 발하임으로 나가, 저녁거리로 쓸 완두콩을 손수 뜰에서 따네.

translation.en: I sit down to shell them, reading my Homer between handfuls.
translation.kr: 앉아서 콩을 까며, 한 움큼씩 까는 사이사이 내 호메로스를 읽지.

translation.en: Then I pick a saucepan out of the kitchen, fetch my own butter, put my mess on the fire, cover it up, and sit stirring it as it needs.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 부엌에서 냄비를 하나 골라 내 버터를 가져다가, 죽을 불에 올리고 뚜껑을 덮고 앉아 필요할 때마다 저어 주네.

translation.en: And I picture to myself the illustrious suitors of Penelope, killing and dressing and cooking their own oxen and swine.
translation.kr: 그러면서 페넬로페의 그 쟁쟁한 구혼자들이 제 손으로 소와 돼지를 잡아 다듬어 요리하던 모습을 떠올리네.

translation.en: Nothing fills me with a purer or more genuine sense of happiness than these touches of patriarchal life which — thank Heaven — I can imitate without affectation.
translation.kr: 이렇게 족장 시대의 자취를 조금이나마 흉내 내는 것만큼 순수하고 참된 행복을 주는 것은 없네. 다행히도 나는 그것을 꾸밈없이 해낼 수 있지.

translation.en: It is a happy thing for me that my heart can feel the same simple, innocent pleasure as the peasant whose table is covered with food he grew himself.
translation.kr: 제 손으로 기른 것으로 상을 차린 농부와 똑같이 소박하고 순진한 기쁨을 내 마음이 느낄 수 있다는 것은 내게 다행한 일일세.

translation.en: He does not merely enjoy his meal.
translation.kr: 그는 그저 밥을 맛있게 먹는 데서 그치지 않네.

translation.en: He remembers with delight the happy days and sunny mornings when he planted it, the soft evenings when he watered it, and the pleasure of watching it grow day by day.
translation.kr: 그것을 심던 행복한 날들과 볕 좋은 아침들, 물을 주던 부드러운 저녁들, 그리고 하루하루 자라는 것을 지켜보던 기쁨까지 흐뭇하게 떠올리지.

translation.en: June 29
translation.kr: 6월 29일

raw: The day before yesterday, the physician came from the town to pay a visit to the judge. He found me on the floor playing with Charlotte's children. Some of them were scrambling over me, and others romped with me; and, as I caught and tickled them, they made a great noise. The doctor is a formal sort of personage: he adjusts the plaits of his ruffles, and continually settles his frill whilst he is talking to you; and he thought my conduct beneath the dignity of a sensible man. I could perceive this by his countenance. But I did not suffer myself to be disturbed. I allowed him to continue his wise conversation, whilst I rebuilt the children's card houses for them as fast as they threw them down. He went about the town afterward, complaining that the judge's children were spoiled enough before, but that now Werther was completely ruining them.

translation.en: The day before yesterday the physician came out from the town to visit the judge.
translation.kr: 그저께 의사가 마을에서 법관을 보러 왔네.

translation.en: He found me on the floor playing with Charlotte's children.
translation.kr: 와 보니 나는 바닥에 엎드려 샤를로테의 동생들과 놀고 있었지.

translation.en: Some of them were scrambling over me and others were romping with me, and as I caught and tickled them they made a great noise.
translation.kr: 몇은 내 등에 기어오르고 몇은 나와 뒹굴었는데, 내가 붙잡아 간질이니 아이들이 어찌나 소란을 피우던지.

translation.en: The doctor is a formal sort of person.
translation.kr: 그 의사는 격식을 몹시 차리는 사람일세.

translation.en: He arranges the pleats of his ruffles and keeps settling his frill while he talks to you.
translation.kr: 말하는 내내 소맷부리 주름을 매만지고 가슴 장식을 연신 바로잡는 그런 사람이지.

translation.en: He thought my behaviour beneath the dignity of a sensible man; I could see it in his face.
translation.kr: 그는 내 행동이 지각 있는 사람의 품위에 어울리지 않는다고 여겼네. 얼굴에 그렇게 쓰여 있었으니.

translation.en: But I did not let myself be disturbed.
translation.kr: 그러나 나는 개의치 않았네.

translation.en: I let him go on with his wise conversation while I rebuilt the children's card houses for them as fast as they knocked them down.
translation.kr: 그가 제 현명한 이야기를 늘어놓게 내버려 두고, 나는 아이들이 무너뜨리는 족족 카드집을 다시 세워 주었네.

translation.en: Afterwards he went about the town complaining that the judge's children were spoiled enough before, but that now Werther was ruining them completely.
translation.kr: 그 뒤 그는 온 마을을 돌아다니며 이렇게 떠들었다네. 법관 댁 아이들은 가뜩이나 버릇이 없었는데 이제 베르테르가 아주 망쳐 놓고 있다고.

raw: Yes, my dear Wilhelm, nothing on this earth affects my heart so much as children. When I look on at their doings; when I mark in the little creatures the seeds of all those virtues and qualities which they will one day find so indispensable; when I behold in the obstinate all the future firmness and constancy of a noble character; in the capricious, that levity and gaiety of temper which will carry them lightly over the dangers and troubles of life, their whole nature simple and unpolluted,—then I call to mind the golden words of the Great Teacher of mankind, "Unless ye become like one of these!" And now, my friend, these children, who are our equals, whom we ought to consider as our models, we treat them as though they were our subjects. They are allowed no will of their own. And have we, then, none ourselves? Whence comes our exclusive right? Is it because we are older and more experienced? Great God! from the height of thy heaven thou beholdest great children and little children, and no others; and thy Son has long since declared which afford thee greatest pleasure. But they believe in him, and hear him not,—that, too, is an old story; and they train their children after their own image, etc.

translation.en: Yes, my dear Wilhelm, nothing on this earth touches my heart like children.
translation.kr: 그렇다네, 친애하는 빌헬름. 이 땅에서 아이들만큼 내 마음을 울리는 것은 없네.

translation.en: When I watch what they do, I see in these little creatures the seeds of every virtue and quality they will one day need so badly.
translation.kr: 아이들이 하는 양을 지켜보면, 이 작은 것들 안에서 언젠가 그토록 절실히 필요하게 될 온갖 덕과 자질의 씨앗이 보이네.

translation.en: In the stubborn one I see the future firmness and constancy of a noble character.
translation.kr: 고집 센 아이에게서는 장차 고결한 성품이 될 굳셈과 한결같음이 보이네.

translation.en: In the capricious one I see the lightness and gaiety of temper that will carry him easily over the dangers and troubles of life.
translation.kr: 변덕스러운 아이에게서는 삶의 위험과 고난을 가볍게 넘어가게 해 줄 경쾌함과 명랑함이 보이지.

translation.en: Their whole nature is simple and unspoiled.
translation.kr: 그 천성은 통째로 소박하고 때 묻지 않았네.

translation.en: And then I call to mind the golden words of the Great Teacher of mankind: "Unless you become like one of these!"
translation.kr: 그러면 나는 인류의 위대한 스승이 남긴 그 금 같은 말씀을 떠올리네. "너희가 이들 가운데 하나와 같이 되지 않으면!"

translation.en: And now, my friend, these children, who are our equals, whom we ought to take as our models — we treat them as though they were our subjects.
translation.kr: 그런데 친구여, 우리와 동등하고 우리가 본받아야 마땅한 이 아이들을, 우리는 마치 신하라도 되는 양 다루고 있네.

translation.en: They are allowed no will of their own.
translation.kr: 아이들에게는 제 뜻이라는 것이 허락되지 않지.

translation.en: And have we none ourselves?
translation.kr: 그렇다면 우리에게는 제 뜻이 있는가?

translation.en: Where does our exclusive right come from?
translation.kr: 그 독점적인 권리는 어디서 온 것인가?

translation.en: Is it because we are older and more experienced?
translation.kr: 우리가 나이가 많고 겪은 것이 많아서인가?

translation.en: Great God, from the height of your heaven you see great children and little children and no others; and your Son declared long ago which of them give you the most pleasure.
translation.kr: 위대한 신이여, 당신의 높은 하늘에서 내려다보시면 큰 아이와 작은 아이가 있을 뿐 다른 것은 없으며, 그 가운데 누가 당신을 가장 기쁘게 하는지는 당신의 아드님이 오래전에 일러 주셨나이다.

translation.en: But they believe in him and do not listen to him — that too is an old story; and they bring up their children in their own image, and so on.
translation.kr: 그러나 사람들은 그를 믿는다면서 그의 말은 듣지 않네. 이 또한 해묵은 이야기지. 그러면서 제 아이들을 제 모습대로 길러 내네.

raw: Adieu, Wilhelm: I will not further bewilder myself with this subject.

translation.en: Goodbye, Wilhelm; I will not tangle myself any further in this subject.
translation.kr: 잘 있게, 빌헬름. 이 문제로 더 뒤엉키지는 않겠네.

translation.en: July 1
translation.kr: 7월 1일

raw: The consolation Charlotte can bring to an invalid I experience from my own heart, which suffers more from her absence than many a poor creature lingering on a bed of sickness. She is gone to spend a few days in the town with a very worthy woman, who is given over by the physicians, and wishes to have Charlotte near her in her last moments. I accompanied her last week on a visit to the Vicar of S—, a small village in the mountains, about a league hence. We arrived about four o'clock: Charlotte had taken her little sister with her. When we entered the vicarage court, we found the good old man sitting on a bench before the door, under the shade of two large walnut-trees. At the sight of Charlotte he seemed to gain new life, rose, forgot his stick, and ventured to walk toward her. She ran to him, and made him sit down again; then, placing herself by his side, she gave him a number of messages from her father, and then caught up his youngest child, a dirty, ugly little thing, the joy of his old age, and kissed it. I wish you could have witnessed her attention to this old man,—how she raised her voice on account of his deafness; how she told him of healthy young people, who had been carried off when it was least expected; praised the virtues of Carlsbad, and commended his determination to spend the ensuing summer there; and assured him that he looked better and stronger than he did when she saw him last. I, in the meantime, paid attention to his good lady. The old man seemed quite in spirits; and as I could not help admiring the beauty of the walnut-trees, which formed such an agreeable shade over our heads, he began, though with some little difficulty, to tell us their history. "As to the oldest," said he, "we do not know who planted it,—some say one clergyman, and some another: but the younger one, there behind us, is exactly the age of my wife, fifty years old next October; her father planted it in the morning, and in the evening she came into the world. My wife's father was my predecessor here, and I cannot tell you how fond he was of that tree; and it is fully as dear to me. Under the shade of that very tree, upon a log of wood, my wife was seated knitting, when I, a poor student, came into this court for the first time, just seven and twenty years ago." Charlotte inquired for his daughter. He said she was gone with Herr Schmidt to the meadows, and was with the haymakers. The old man then resumed his story, and told us how his predecessor had taken a fancy to him, as had his daughter likewise; and how he had become first his curate, and subsequently his successor. He had scarcely finished his story when his daughter returned through the garden, accompanied by the above-mentioned Herr Schmidt. She welcomed Charlotte affectionately, and I confess I was much taken with her appearance. She was a lively-looking, good-humoured brunette, quite competent to amuse one for a short time in the country. Her lover (for such Herr Schmidt evidently appeared to be) was a polite, reserved personage, and would not join our conversation, notwithstanding all Charlotte's endeavours to draw him out. I was much annoyed at observing, by his countenance, that his silence did not arise from want of talent, but from caprice and ill-humour. This subsequently became very evident, when we set out to take a walk, and Frederica joining Charlotte, with whom I was talking, the worthy gentleman's face, which was naturally rather sombre, became so dark and angry that Charlotte was obliged to touch my arm, and remind me that I was talking too much to Frederica. Nothing distresses me more than to see men torment each other; particularly when in the flower of their age, in the very season of pleasure, they waste their few short days of sunshine in quarrels and disputes, and only perceive their error when it is too late to repair it. This thought dwelt upon my mind; and in the evening, when we returned to the vicar's, and were sitting round the table with our bread and milk, the conversation turned on the joys and sorrows of the world, I could not resist the temptation to inveigh bitterly against ill-humour. "We are apt," said I, "to complain, but—with very little cause, that our happy days are few, and our evil days many. If our hearts were always disposed to receive the benefits Heaven sends us, we should acquire strength to support evil when it comes." "But," observed the vicar's wife, "we cannot always command our tempers, so much depends upon the constitution: when the body suffers, the mind is ill at ease." "I acknowledge that," I continued; "but we must consider such a disposition in the light of a disease, and inquire whether there is no remedy for it."

translation.en: The comfort Charlotte can bring to an invalid I feel in my own heart, which suffers more from her absence than many a poor creature lying on a sickbed.
translation.kr: 샤를로테가 병자에게 줄 수 있는 위안이 어떤 것인지를 나는 내 마음으로 느끼고 있네. 그 사람이 없어서 앓는 내 마음이 병상에 누운 어느 가엾은 이보다 더 아프니 말일세.

translation.en: She has gone to spend a few days in the town with a very worthy woman whom the doctors have given up, and who wants Charlotte near her at the end.
translation.kr: 그 사람은 의사들이 이미 손을 놓은 어느 훌륭한 부인 곁에서 며칠을 보내려고 마을에 갔네. 그 부인이 마지막을 샤를로테와 함께하고 싶어 한다는군.

translation.en: Last week I went with her to visit the Vicar of S—, a small village in the mountains about a league from here.
translation.kr: 지난주에는 그 사람과 함께 여기서 십 리쯤 떨어진 산속 작은 마을, S—의 목사를 뵈러 갔었네.

translation.en: We arrived around four o'clock.
translation.kr: 네 시쯤 도착했네.

translation.en: Charlotte had brought her little sister with her.
translation.kr: 샤를로테는 어린 동생을 데리고 갔지.

translation.en: When we came into the vicarage courtyard we found the good old man sitting on a bench before the door, in the shade of two large walnut-trees.
translation.kr: 목사관 안뜰에 들어서니, 그 마음씨 좋은 노인이 커다란 호두나무 두 그루 그늘 아래 문 앞 의자에 앉아 있더군.

translation.en: At the sight of Charlotte he seemed to gain new life: he got up, forgot his stick, and ventured to walk toward her.
translation.kr: 샤를로테를 보자 노인은 새 기운을 얻은 듯했네. 자리에서 일어나 지팡이도 잊은 채 그쪽으로 걸어오려 했지.

translation.en: She ran to him and made him sit down again.
translation.kr: 그 사람은 달려가 노인을 다시 앉혔네.

translation.en: Then she took a place beside him, gave him a number of messages from her father, and caught up his youngest child — a dirty, ugly little thing, the joy of his old age — and kissed it.
translation.kr: 그러고는 곁에 자리를 잡고 아버지의 안부를 여러 가지 전한 다음, 노인의 막내아이를 — 꾀죄죄하고 못생겼지만 노년의 기쁨인 그 아이를 — 안아 올려 입을 맞추었네.

translation.en: I wish you could have seen her attention to that old man.
translation.kr: 그 노인을 대하는 그 사람의 살뜰함을 자네도 보았더라면 좋았을 텐데.

translation.en: She raised her voice because he is deaf; she told him of healthy young people carried off when no one expected it; she praised the virtues of Carlsbad and approved his plan to spend next summer there.
translation.kr: 귀가 어두우시니 목소리를 높여 드리고, 뜻밖에 세상을 떠난 젊고 건강한 이들 이야기를 들려 드리고, 카를스바트 온천의 효험을 칭찬하며 다음 여름에 거기서 지내시겠다는 계획을 잘하셨다고 해 드렸네.

translation.en: And she assured him that he looked better and stronger than when she last saw him.
translation.kr: 그리고 지난번에 뵈었을 때보다 안색도 좋고 기운도 나아 보이신다고 안심시켜 드렸지.

translation.en: Meanwhile I paid my attentions to his good lady.
translation.kr: 그동안 나는 그 부인을 살펴 드렸네.

translation.en: The old man was in high spirits; and since I could not help admiring the beauty of the walnut-trees that cast such a pleasant shade over our heads, he began — with some little difficulty — to tell us their history.
translation.kr: 노인은 기분이 아주 좋아 보였네. 우리 머리 위로 그토록 기분 좋은 그늘을 드리운 호두나무의 아름다움을 내가 감탄하지 않을 수 없자, 노인은 좀 힘겨워하면서도 그 나무들의 내력을 들려주기 시작했네.

translation.en: "As to the older one," he said, "we do not know who planted it; some say one clergyman, some another."
translation.kr: "나이 든 쪽은" 하고 노인이 말했네. "누가 심었는지 모른다오. 어느 목사라고도 하고 또 다른 목사라고도 하지요."

translation.en: "But the younger one, there behind us, is exactly my wife's age: fifty years old next October."
translation.kr: "그러나 우리 뒤에 있는 저 젊은 쪽은 내 아내와 나이가 꼭 같소. 오는 시월이면 쉰이 되지요."

translation.en: "Her father planted it in the morning, and in the evening she came into the world."
translation.kr: "그 애 아버지가 아침에 저것을 심었고, 저녁에 그 애가 세상에 나왔다오."

translation.en: "My wife's father was my predecessor here, and I cannot tell you how fond he was of that tree; it is quite as dear to me."
translation.kr: "내 아내의 아버지가 여기 내 전임자였는데, 저 나무를 얼마나 아꼈는지 말로 다 할 수 없소. 내게도 그만큼 소중하지요."

translation.en: "My wife was sitting under that very tree, on a log of wood, knitting, when I came into this courtyard for the first time as a poor student — just twenty-seven years ago."
translation.kr: "바로 저 나무 아래 통나무에 앉아 뜨개질을 하고 있던 것이 내 아내였소. 내가 가난한 학생으로 이 뜰에 처음 들어섰을 때 말이오. 꼭 스물일곱 해 전이라오."

translation.en: Charlotte asked after his daughter.
translation.kr: 샤를로테가 노인의 딸을 찾았네.

translation.en: He said she had gone with Herr Schmidt to the meadows, and was out with the haymakers.
translation.kr: 노인은 딸이 슈미트 씨와 초원에 나가 풀 베는 사람들과 함께 있다고 했네.

translation.en: The old man took up his story again, and told us how his predecessor had taken a liking to him, and his daughter likewise, and how he had become first the man's curate and then his successor.
translation.kr: 노인은 다시 이야기를 이어, 전임자가 자기를 마음에 들어 했고 그 딸 또한 그러했으며, 그래서 자기가 먼저 그 사람의 부목사가 되었다가 뒤를 잇게 되었다고 들려주었네.

translation.en: He had hardly finished when his daughter came back through the garden, together with the Herr Schmidt he had mentioned.
translation.kr: 이야기를 마치기가 무섭게 딸이 뜰을 가로질러 돌아왔는데, 방금 말한 그 슈미트 씨와 함께였네.

translation.en: She welcomed Charlotte affectionately, and I confess I was much taken with the look of her.
translation.kr: 그 여자는 샤를로테를 다정하게 맞이했고, 솔직히 말해 나도 그 모습이 꽤 마음에 들었네.

translation.en: She was a lively, good-humoured brunette, quite capable of amusing one for a short stay in the country.
translation.kr: 활기차고 명랑한 갈색 머리 아가씨였는데, 시골에 잠시 머무는 동안 말동무 삼기에는 충분한 사람이었지.

translation.en: Her lover — for that is plainly what Herr Schmidt was — was a polite, reserved person who would not join our conversation, for all Charlotte's efforts to draw him out.
translation.kr: 그 연인은 — 슈미트 씨가 그런 사이인 것은 분명했네 — 예의는 바르나 말수가 적은 사람이라, 샤를로테가 아무리 끌어내려 애써도 우리 이야기에 끼려 하지 않았네.

translation.en: What annoyed me was to see in his face that his silence came not from any want of ability, but from caprice and ill humour.
translation.kr: 나를 언짢게 한 것은, 그 침묵이 능력이 모자라서가 아니라 변덕과 심술에서 나온 것임이 얼굴에 드러나 보였다는 점일세.

translation.en: This became very plain later, when we set out for a walk and Frederica joined Charlotte, with whom I was talking.
translation.kr: 그것은 나중에 아주 분명해졌네. 우리가 산책을 나섰을 때 프레데리카가 나와 이야기하던 샤를로테 곁으로 왔거든.

translation.en: The worthy gentleman's face, which is naturally rather sombre, went so dark and angry that Charlotte had to touch my arm and remind me I was talking too much to Frederica.
translation.kr: 본래도 좀 침침한 그 훌륭하신 분의 얼굴이 어찌나 어둡고 성나 보이던지, 샤를로테가 내 팔을 건드리며 프레데리카와 너무 많이 이야기한다고 일러 줄 정도였네.

translation.en: Nothing distresses me more than to see people torment one another.
translation.kr: 사람들이 서로를 괴롭히는 것을 보는 것만큼 나를 슬프게 하는 일은 없네.

translation.en: Worst of all when they are in the flower of their age, in the very season of pleasure, and waste their few short days of sunshine in quarrels and disputes, and only see their mistake when it is too late to repair it.
translation.kr: 무엇보다 한창때, 즐거움을 누릴 바로 그 철에, 몇 안 되는 볕 좋은 날들을 다툼과 언쟁으로 허비하다가, 돌이킬 수 없게 되고서야 제 잘못을 깨닫는 것을 볼 때 그렇지.

translation.en: The thought stayed with me; and in the evening, when we came back to the vicar's and sat round the table with our bread and milk, the talk turned to the joys and sorrows of the world.
translation.kr: 그 생각이 내내 떠나지 않았네. 저녁에 목사관으로 돌아와 빵과 우유를 놓고 둘러앉았을 때, 이야기는 세상의 기쁨과 슬픔으로 흘러갔네.

translation.en: I could not resist speaking bitterly against ill humour.
translation.kr: 나는 심술궂은 성미에 대해 모질게 말하지 않을 수 없었네.

translation.en: "We are apt to complain," I said, "though with very little cause, that our happy days are few and our evil days many."
translation.kr: "우리는 곧잘 푸념합니다." 내가 말했네. "별로 그럴 까닭도 없으면서, 좋은 날은 적고 궂은 날은 많다고 말이지요."

translation.en: "If our hearts were always ready to receive the good that Heaven sends us, we should gain the strength to bear the evil when it comes."
translation.kr: "하늘이 보내 주시는 좋은 것을 늘 받아들일 마음이 되어 있다면, 궂은 일이 닥쳤을 때 견딜 힘도 얻게 될 것입니다."

translation.en: "But we cannot always command our tempers," said the vicar's wife. "So much depends on the constitution: when the body suffers, the mind is ill at ease."
translation.kr: "그러나 사람이 늘 제 성미를 다스릴 수는 없지요." 목사 부인이 말했네. "타고난 몸에 달린 것이 많으니까요. 몸이 괴로우면 마음도 편치 않은 법이에요."

translation.en: "I grant that," I went on, "but we must treat such a disposition as a disease, and ask whether there is no remedy for it."
translation.kr: "그 점은 인정합니다." 내가 말을 이었네. "그러나 그런 기질은 병으로 보아야 하고, 거기에 약이 없는지 물어야 합니다."

raw: "I should be glad to hear one," said Charlotte: "at least, I think very much depends upon ourselves; I know it is so with me. When anything annoys me, and disturbs my temper, I hasten into the garden, hum a couple of country dances, and it is all right with me directly." "That is what I meant," I replied; "ill-humour resembles indolence: it is natural to us; but if once we have courage to exert ourselves, we find our work run fresh from our hands, and we experience in the activity from which we shrank a real enjoyment." Frederica listened very attentively: and the young man objected, that we were not masters of ourselves, and still less so of our feelings. "The question is about a disagreeable feeling," I added, "from which every one would willingly escape, but none know their own power without trial. Invalids are glad to consult physicians, and submit to the most scrupulous regimen, the most nauseous medicines, in order to recover their health." I observed that the good old man inclined his head, and exerted himself to hear our discourse; so I raised my voice, and addressed myself directly to him. "We preach against a great many crimes," I observed, "but I never remember a sermon delivered against ill-humour." "That may do very well for your town clergymen," said he: "country people are never ill-humoured; though, indeed, it might be useful, occasionally, to my wife for instance, and the judge." We all laughed, as did he likewise very cordially, till he fell into a fit of coughing, which interrupted our conversation for a time. Herr Schmidt resumed the subject. "You call ill humour a crime," he remarked, "but I think you use too strong a term." "Not at all," I replied, "if that deserves the name which is so pernicious to ourselves and our neighbours. Is it not enough that we want the power to make one another happy, must we deprive each other of the pleasure which we can all make for ourselves? Show me the man who has the courage to hide his ill-humour, who bears the whole burden himself, without disturbing the peace of those around him. No: ill-humour arises from an inward consciousness of our own want of merit, from a discontent which ever accompanies that envy which foolish vanity engenders. We see people happy, whom we have not made so, and cannot endure the sight." Charlotte looked at me with a smile; she observed the emotion with which I spoke: and a tear in the eyes of Frederica stimulated me to proceed. "Woe unto those," I said, "who use their power over a human heart to destroy the simple pleasures it would naturally enjoy! All the favours, all the attentions, in the world cannot compensate for the loss of that happiness which a cruel tyranny has destroyed." My heart was full as I spoke. A recollection of many things which had happened pressed upon my mind, and filled my eyes with tears. "We should daily repeat to ourselves," I exclaimed, "that we should not interfere with our friends, unless to leave them in possession of their own joys, and increase their happiness by sharing it with them! But when their souls are tormented by a violent passion, or their hearts rent with grief, is it in your power to afford them the slightest consolation?

translation.en: "I should be glad to hear of one," said Charlotte. "At least, I think a great deal depends on ourselves; I know it does with me."
translation.kr: "약이 있다면 저도 듣고 싶군요." 샤를로테가 말했네. "적어도 많은 것이 우리 자신에게 달렸다고는 생각해요. 저는 그렇거든요."

translation.en: "When something annoys me and upsets my temper, I hurry into the garden, hum a couple of country dances, and it is all right with me at once."
translation.kr: "무언가 거슬려 마음이 상하면 얼른 뜰로 나가 춤곡을 두어 가락 흥얼거려요. 그러면 곧 괜찮아지지요."

translation.en: "That is just what I meant," I replied. "Ill humour is like laziness: it comes naturally to us."
translation.kr: "바로 제가 하려던 말입니다." 내가 답했네. "심술은 게으름과 같습니다. 우리에게 절로 생기는 것이지요."

translation.en: "But once we have the courage to rouse ourselves, the work runs fresh from our hands, and we find real enjoyment in the very activity we shrank from."
translation.kr: "그러나 한번 떨치고 일어날 용기를 내면, 일이 손끝에서 새로 풀려 나오고, 꺼리던 바로 그 움직임 속에서 참된 즐거움을 찾게 됩니다."

translation.en: Frederica listened very attentively, and the young man objected that we are not masters of ourselves, and still less of our feelings.
translation.kr: 프레데리카는 아주 귀 기울여 듣고 있었고, 그 젊은이는 우리가 우리 자신의 주인이 못 되며 감정은 더더욱 그렇다고 반박했네.

translation.en: "What we are talking about is a disagreeable feeling," I added, "which everyone would gladly escape; but nobody knows his own power until he has tried it."
translation.kr: "우리가 말하는 것은 언짢은 기분입니다." 내가 덧붙였네. "누구나 기꺼이 벗어나고 싶어 하는 것이지요. 그러나 해 보기 전에는 아무도 제 힘을 알지 못합니다."

translation.en: "A sick man is glad to consult his physician, and will submit to the strictest regimen and the most nauseous medicines in order to get his health back."
translation.kr: "병든 사람은 기꺼이 의사를 찾고, 건강을 되찾으려고 가장 엄한 섭생과 가장 역겨운 약도 마다하지 않습니다."

translation.en: I noticed the good old man leaning forward, straining to hear our talk, so I raised my voice and spoke directly to him.
translation.kr: 그 마음씨 좋은 노인이 몸을 기울여 우리 이야기를 애써 들으려 하기에, 나는 목소리를 높여 그분에게 바로 말을 건넸네.

translation.en: "We preach against a great many crimes," I said, "but I cannot remember ever hearing a sermon preached against ill humour."
translation.kr: "우리는 온갖 죄악에 대해 설교합니다." 내가 말했네. "그러나 심술에 대한 설교는 들어 본 기억이 없습니다."

translation.en: "That may do very well for your town clergymen," he said. "Country people are never ill-humoured — though it might be useful now and then, to my wife for instance, and to the judge."
translation.kr: "그것은 도시 목사들에게나 어울릴 이야기지요." 노인이 말했네. "시골 사람들은 심술을 부리는 법이 없으니까요. 하기야 이따금 쓸모가 있기는 하겠소. 이를테면 내 아내라든가, 저 법관 양반에게는."

translation.en: We all laughed, and he laughed very cordially himself, until he fell into a fit of coughing that interrupted our conversation for a time.
translation.kr: 우리는 모두 웃었고, 노인 자신도 아주 흔쾌히 웃다가 기침이 터져 한동안 이야기가 끊겼네.

translation.en: Herr Schmidt took the subject up again.
translation.kr: 슈미트 씨가 그 이야기를 다시 집어 들었네.

translation.en: "You call ill humour a crime," he remarked, "but I think you use too strong a term."
translation.kr: "심술을 죄악이라 하시는데" 하고 그가 말했네. "그 말은 너무 지나친 것 같군요."

translation.en: "Not at all," I replied, "if the name belongs to anything so harmful to ourselves and to our neighbours."
translation.kr: "조금도 지나치지 않습니다." 내가 답했네. "우리 자신과 이웃에게 그토록 해로운 것이라면 그 이름이 마땅하지요."

translation.en: "Is it not enough that we lack the power to make one another happy?"
translation.kr: "서로를 행복하게 해 줄 힘이 없는 것만으로도 모자랍니까?"

translation.en: "Must we rob each other of the pleasure we can all make for ourselves?"
translation.kr: "우리가 스스로 만들어 낼 수 있는 즐거움마저 서로에게서 빼앗아야 합니까?"

translation.en: "Show me the man who has the courage to hide his ill humour, who carries the whole burden of it himself without disturbing the peace of those around him."
translation.kr: "제 심술을 감출 용기를 지닌 사람, 그 짐을 혼자 다 지고 둘레 사람들의 평온을 흔들지 않는 사람을 제게 보여 주십시오."

translation.en: "No: ill humour comes from an inward sense of our own want of merit, from a discontent that always goes with the envy that foolish vanity breeds."
translation.kr: "아닙니다. 심술은 제 못남을 속으로 아는 데서, 그리고 어리석은 허영이 낳는 시샘에 늘 따라붙는 불만에서 나옵니다."

translation.en: "We see people happy whom we have not made so, and we cannot bear the sight."
translation.kr: "우리가 행복하게 해 준 것도 아닌 사람들이 행복한 것을 보면서, 우리는 그 꼴을 견디지 못하는 것이지요."

translation.en: Charlotte looked at me with a smile; she had seen the feeling with which I spoke, and a tear in Frederica's eyes urged me on.
translation.kr: 샤를로테는 웃음 띤 얼굴로 나를 바라보았네. 내가 어떤 감정으로 말하는지 알아본 것이지. 그리고 프레데리카의 눈에 맺힌 눈물이 나를 더 밀어붙였네.

translation.en: "Woe to those," I said, "who use their power over a human heart to destroy the simple pleasures it would naturally enjoy!"
translation.kr: "화 있을진저." 내가 말했네. "사람의 마음에 대한 제 힘을 써서, 그 마음이 절로 누릴 소박한 즐거움을 부수는 자들이여!"

translation.en: "All the favours and all the attentions in the world cannot make up for the loss of a happiness that a cruel tyranny has destroyed."
translation.kr: "세상의 온갖 호의와 온갖 배려로도, 모진 횡포가 부숴 버린 행복의 자리를 메울 수는 없습니다."

translation.en: My heart was full as I spoke.
translation.kr: 말하는 동안 내 가슴은 벅차올랐네.

translation.en: The memory of many things that had happened pressed on my mind and filled my eyes with tears.
translation.kr: 지난 일들의 기억이 마음을 짓눌러 눈에 눈물이 고였네.

translation.en: "We ought to say to ourselves every day," I cried, "that we should not interfere with our friends, except to leave them in possession of their own joys and to increase their happiness by sharing it with them!"
translation.kr: "우리는 날마다 스스로에게 일러야 합니다." 내가 외쳤네. "벗들의 일에 끼어들지 말 것, 다만 그들이 제 기쁨을 그대로 누리게 두고 그것을 함께 나누어 그 행복을 키워 줄 때가 아니면!"

translation.en: "But when their souls are tormented by a violent passion, or their hearts torn with grief, is it in your power to give them the slightest consolation?"
translation.kr: "그러나 그 영혼이 격렬한 정념에 시달리고 그 가슴이 슬픔으로 찢길 때, 그대에게 그들을 조금이라도 위로할 힘이 있습니까?"

raw: "And when the last fatal malady seizes the being whose untimely grave you have prepared, when she lies languid and exhausted before you, her dim eyes raised to heaven, and the damp of death upon her pallid brow, there you stand at her bedside like a condemned criminal, with the bitter feeling that your whole fortune could not save her; and the agonising thought wrings you, that all your efforts are powerless to impart even a moment's strength to the departing soul, or quicken her with a transitory consolation."

translation.en: "And then comes the last fatal illness, seizing the creature whose untimely grave you yourself prepared."
translation.kr: "그러다 마지막 치명적인 병이 찾아옵니다. 그대가 스스로 이른 무덤을 마련해 준 그 사람을 덮치는 것이지요."

translation.en: "She lies before you, weak and exhausted, her dim eyes raised to heaven, the damp of death on her pale forehead."
translation.kr: "그 사람은 그대 앞에 누워 있습니다. 지치고 기운이 다한 채, 흐려진 눈을 하늘로 들고, 창백한 이마에 죽음의 땀이 배어 있습니다."

translation.en: "And there you stand at her bedside like a condemned criminal, with the bitter knowledge that your whole fortune could not save her."
translation.kr: "그리고 그대는 사형수처럼 그 머리맡에 서 있습니다. 제 전 재산으로도 그 사람을 살릴 수 없다는 쓰디쓴 앎을 안고서."

translation.en: "And the agonising thought wrings you, that all your efforts are powerless to give the departing soul a moment's strength, or to quicken her with even a passing consolation."
translation.kr: "그리고 애타는 생각이 그대를 쥐어짭니다. 그대의 온갖 애씀으로도 떠나가는 그 영혼에 한순간의 힘도, 스쳐 가는 위안 하나도 줄 수 없다는 생각이."

raw: At these words the remembrance of a similar scene at which I had been once present fell with full force upon my heart. I buried my face in my handkerchief, and hastened from the room, and was only recalled to my recollection by Charlotte's voice, who reminded me that it was time to return home. With what tenderness she chid me on the way for the too eager interest I took in everything! She declared it would do me injury, and that I ought to spare myself. Yes, my angel! I will do so for your sake.

translation.en: At these words the memory of a scene like it, which I had once witnessed myself, fell on my heart with full force.
translation.kr: 이 말에, 전에 내가 직접 겪었던 비슷한 장면의 기억이 온 힘으로 내 가슴을 덮쳤네.

translation.en: I buried my face in my handkerchief and hurried out of the room.
translation.kr: 나는 손수건에 얼굴을 파묻고 방을 뛰쳐나왔네.

translation.en: I was brought back to myself only by Charlotte's voice, reminding me that it was time to go home.
translation.kr: 이제 집에 갈 시간이라고 이르는 샤를로테의 목소리에야 겨우 정신이 돌아왔네.

translation.en: How tenderly she scolded me on the way for the too eager interest I take in everything!
translation.kr: 돌아오는 길에 그 사람이 무슨 일에나 너무 뜨겁게 마음을 쏟는다고 나를 나무라는데, 그 다정함이라니!

translation.en: She said it would do me harm, and that I ought to spare myself.
translation.kr: 그러다 몸을 상하니 좀 아끼라고 하더군.

translation.en: Yes, my angel!
translation.kr: 그러네, 나의 천사여!

translation.en: I will do so for your sake.
translation.kr: 그대를 위해서라면 그리하겠네.
